title: Policy Learning with Observational Data: The Case of Hepatitis C Treatment for HIV/HCV Co-Infected Patients
abstract: arXiv:2605.16593v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Decision-makers frequently must choose a single action from a finite set of alternatives -- for example, physicians selecting a treatment, investors choosing a portfolio risk level, or judges determining sentences. To improve outcomes, policymakers often issue policy rules or guidelines to inform such choices. In this paper, I show how to generally derive policy rules from observational data in a multi-action framework under relatively weak assumptions about the underlying structure of the heterogeneous sampled population. Conditional average treatment effects (CATEs) are consistently estimated via a weighted K-means algorithm, assuming the outcome model is correctly specified within each homogeneous subgroup. I then use standard decision trees to implement feasible policy rules, allowing for both perfect and imperfect adherence to treatment. The methodology is applied to treatment options for Hepatitis C (HCV) among patients c

translated_title: 基于观测数据的政策学习：HIV/HCV合并感染患者丙型肝炎治疗的案例研究
translated_abstract: 决策者经常必须从有限的一组备选方案中做出单一选择——例如，医生选择治疗方案、投资者选择投资组合的风险水平，或法官决定量刑。为了改善结果，政策制定者通常会发布政策规则或指南来指导此类选择。在本文中，作者展示了如何在多行动框架下、在对异质性抽样人群底层结构假设相对较弱的情况下，从观测数据中普遍推导政策规则。在假设结果模型在每个同质子群内被正确设定的条件下，通过加权K-means算法一致地估计条件平均处理效应（CATE）。随后，作者使用标准决策树来实现可行的政策规则，并同时考虑了完全依从治疗与不完全依从治疗两种情形。该方法被应用于HIV/HCV合并感染患者的丙型肝炎（HCV）治疗方案选择。
tldr: 本文提出了一种在较弱假设下从观测数据推导多行动政策规则的方法，通过加权K-means算法估计条件平均处理效应并结合标准决策树生成可行政策规则，且能处理治疗依从性不完美的情况，并成功应用于HIV/HCV合并感染患者的丙肝治疗方案选择。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a general framework for deriving multi-action policy rules from observational data under weak assumptions, consistently estimating CATEs via a weighted K-means algorithm and implementing feasible policy rules with standard decision trees while accommodating imperfect treatment adherence, applied to Hepatitis C treatment selection for HIV/HCV co-infected patients.
